correctness.rationale: For every finite nonempty simple graph satisfying the formula, the adjacency rows are nonzero, pairwise distinct, and closed under unequal-element XOR. Adjoining zero yields a binary vector space. Evaluation of adjacency induces an alternating nondegenerate bilinear form, hence the graph is Sp(2m,2); bilinearity proves the converse. To prove width optimality, the Abiad--Haemers four-vector switch of Sp(6,2) has 63 vertices and binary rank eight rather than six, so lies outside the characterized class. Both graphs share strongly regular parameters (63,32,16,16), whose pair-neighborhood counts are strictly positive in all four patterns (adjacent: 16,15,15,15; nonadjacent: 16,16,16,13). Thus an unlimited three-pebble matching strategy exists. Independent within-package Python computations replay construction, ranks, extension positivity and exhaustive orders <=5, but finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The specific combined result is a dimension-free four-variable sentence in the bare graph language that recognizes precisely the binary symplectic graph family among ALL finite simple graphs, together with an exact lower bound of four variable names. Abiad--Haemers contain the row-sum nonclosure observation and strongly regular switched graph; Peeters gives a rank-plus-parameters characterization; Kubota has distinct numerical invariants of switched families. Those inspected scientific claims neither state the parameter-free unrestricted-domain first-order characterization nor show the tight three-pebble bound. Searches in the published findings database found no stronger covering claim, but absence of results does not establish novelty; see residual risks.
residual_risks: General graph-theoretic binary representations or algebraic characterizations may already contain the recognition half without explicit logical wording.
An uninspected finite-variable logical composition/interpretation theorem could imply the complete width statement.
Peeters 1995 primary full text was not inspected, and Grohe--Otto was read at abstract level only; no novelty conclusion rests on claims of their whole-document noncoverage.
Published semantic database searches provide no global uniqueness guarantee; independent historical-priority review is unperformed.

value.rationale: Dimension-free finite-variable logical recognition of the entire symplectic graph family from pure adjacency, with an optimal width boundary, is a natural exact structural classification rather than a table lookup. The symplectic form is recovered from graph rows without degree, size, rank or field predicates. A strongly regular switched nonmember shares all one- and two-point adjacency extension behavior, proving exactly why three variables cannot detect the algebraic row structure. Although ingredients are classical, their sharp logical combination is a motivated mathematical boundary; priority risk remains qualified.
